title: Everything that could happen
question: What do we call the list of everything that could happen in a random trial?
hook: Before you can ask how likely something is, you have to say what the possibilities even are.
idea: A sample space is the set of all possible outcomes, and choosing it well depends on what you care about.

beats.prompt: Match each part of a probability model to its job.
pairs: The set of all possible outcomes
A subset of the sample space
Assigns a probability to each event
beats.explain: A probability model has three components: a sample space, a set of possible events, and a probability assigned to each event.

beats.prompt: Two fair six-sided dice are thrown. The 36 ordered pairs are equally likely. What is the chance that the pair adds up to five?

choices.label: 1 in 11
choices.feedback: There are 11 possible sums, but those sums are not equally likely, so this ignores how many pairs make each one.

choices.label: 5 in 36
choices.feedback: The number five is the target sum, not the number of pairs that reach it.

choices.label: 1 in 6
choices.feedback: This would be 6 pairs out of 36, which is more than the four that add to five.

beats.explain: Four of the 36 equally likely ordered pairs add up to five, so the probability is 4/36.

beats.prompt: Sort each experiment by whether its outcomes are naturally equally likely.
items: Ordered pairs from two fair six-sided dice
Each individual card from a standard 52-card deck
Every possible simple random sample of a given size
A thumb tack landing point up or point down
beats.explain: Dice pairs, individual cards and simple random samples are described as equally likely outcomes, while the thumb tack has no symmetry to suggest it.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning about drawing a card is wrong. Which one?
steps: A person drawing a card only cares about the suit.
So the four suits are a possible sample space for them.
So the only valid sample space is all 52 individual cards.
Which sample space fits depends on the result being studied.
beats.explain: There can be more than one plausible sample space, such as ranks, suits or individual cards, depending on what result interests the experimenter.
